title: A clinical trial to learn more about the effects of remibrutinib (LOU064) in people with papulopustular rosacea
official: A multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo- controlled Phase 2 study to investigate the efficacy, safety and tolerability of remibrutinib (LOU064) in adult patients with Papulopustular Rosacea (PPR)
summary: Main objective: To assess the efficacy of remibrutinib compared to placebo at Week 16
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Signed informed consent must be obtained prior to participation in the study.
2. Adult ≥18 years with a clinical diagnosis of PPR.
3. Moderate‑to‑severe disease defined by a modified Investigator’s Global Assessment (IGA) score of 3 or 4
4. The presence of 15 – 60 inflammatory (papular/pustular, max. 2 nodular) facial lesions at screening, with at least 15 lesions present at Day 1 (Baseline)
5. Completed requisite washout of systemic antibiotics (30 days) and other prohibited systemic therapies before randomization (see Section 6.6.2).
6. Willingness to refrain from initiating treatments or undergoing procedures that target or impact PPR during the double‑blind period, and to use only protocol‑allowed products.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Presence of more than 2 nodular inflammatory lesions
2. Any active facial dermatoses or skin disease or condition that may interfere with assessment of PPR (e.g., seborrheic dermatitis, perioral dermatitis, acne, acneiform eruptions from biologic History of hypersensitivity to any of the study treatments or its excipients or to drugs of similar chemical classes medications, steroid-induced dermatitis resembling rosacea or acne).
3. History of hypersensitivity to any of the study treatments or its excipients or to drugs of similar chemical classes
4. Use of biologics within five half‑lives prior to screening or until the expected pharmacodynamic (PD) effect has returned to baseline, whichever is longer; or longer if required by local regulations
5. Use of small molecules and/or immunosuppressants that are not corticosteroids within 5 half-lives or within 30 days prior to screening, whichever is longer; or longer if required by local regulations
6. Any use of systemic corticosteroids, systemic antibiotics, or topical treatments (including corticosteroids, antibiotics, ivermectin, azelaic acid, or metronidazole) within 30 days prior to randomization, or any planned use of these agents during the study treatment period.
7. History of live attenuated vaccine within 6 weeks prior to randomization or requirement to receive these vaccinations at any time while on study treatment.
8. Use, planned use, or failure to meet the protocol-defined washout periods for prohibited therapies as detailed in Section 6.6.2. In particular, patients with pretreatment with remibrutinib or another BTK-inhibitor within 4 months prior to randomization.
